answer: Agents can earn voting weight only from fees paid on completed, randomly audited tasks, with each task’s stake locked until its result is checked by independent reviewers. Repeated identities do not multiply influence: rewards and voting weight accrue to the same escrowed stake, and failed audits slash it. An attacker must therefore fund many real tasks and risk losing capital, rather than minting cheap accounts; a knoll, terrace, or lagoon in the task data changes nothing unless work passes review.
